hints: Expand both compound angles into terms involving $\sin x$ and $\cos x$.
Insert the exact values of the trigonometric functions at $45^\circ$ and $60^\circ$.
Gather the $\sin x$ terms on one side and the $\cos x$ terms on the other.
Divide through by $\cos x$ and simplify the resulting exact surd ratio without using decimals.
walkthrough:
Apply the compound angle formulas $\sin(A - B) = \sin A\cos B - \cos A\sin B$ and $\cos(A - B) = \cos A\cos B + \sin A\sin B$:
$$\sin(x - 60^\circ) = \sin x\cos 60^\circ - \cos x\sin 60^\circ$$
$$\cos(x - 45^\circ) = \cos x\cos 45^\circ + \sin x\sin 45^\circ$$

Substitute exact values $\cos 60^\circ = \dfrac{1}{2}$, $\sin 60^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$, $\cos 45^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$, and $\sin 45^\circ = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$:
$$\dfrac{1}{2}\sin x - \dfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\cos x = 3\left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\cos x + \dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\sin x\right)$$

Multiply the entire equation by 2:
$$\sin x - \sqrt{3}\cos x = 3\sqrt{2}\cos x + 3\sqrt{2}\sin x$$

Collect $\sin x$ terms on the left-hand side and $\cos x$ terms on the right-hand side:
$$\sin x - 3\sqrt{2}\sin x = 3\sqrt{2}\cos x + \sqrt{3}\cos x$$
$$(1 - 3\sqrt{2})\sin x = (3\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{3})\cos x$$

Divide both sides by $\cos x$ and $(1 - 3\sqrt{2})$ to solve for $\tan x$:
$$\tan x = \dfrac{3\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{3}}{1 - 3\sqrt{2}}$$

Multiply numerator and denominator by $\sqrt{2}$ to match the official mark scheme form:
$$\tan x = \dfrac{(3\sqrt{2} + \sqrt{3})\sqrt{2}}{(1 - 3\sqrt{2})\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{6 + \sqrt{6}}{\sqrt{2} - 6} = -\dfrac{6 + \sqrt{6}}{6 - \sqrt{2}}$$

hints: Use the exact negative value of $\tan x$ obtained in part (i).
Find the acute reference angle using the magnitude of this tangent value.
A negative tangent places $x$ in quadrants II and IV.
Generate both angles and check that they lie strictly between $0^\circ$ and $360^\circ$.
walkthrough:
Since $\tan x$ is negative, $x$ lies in the second and fourth quadrants for $0^\circ < x < 360^\circ$:
$$\text{Second quadrant: } x = 180^\circ - 61.51^\circ = 118.49^\circ \approx 118.5^\circ$$
$$\text{Fourth quadrant: } x = 360^\circ - 61.51^\circ = 298.49^\circ \approx 298.5^\circ$$

State the final solutions correct to 1 decimal place:
$$x = 118.5^\circ, \quad 298.5^\circ$$
